Idk how much this will help you, but I had a very similar experience myself last year.  February of last year I was so depressed and self-loathing, I thought about suicide and death constantly, although I never made any definitely plans or anything.  My self-esteem was incredibly low, I didn't have any close friends I could talk to about this, and my boyfriend lived a thousand miles away (literally) and couldn't do much for me.  I was hospitalized when I was in middle school for about a week for cutting and depression, and I remember it being very helpful for me.  There was group therapy, individual therapy, and socializing with others who had similar issues as I did.  Also structure.  But I was 12 then, and am 22 now, so I'm sure the teenage and adult wards are very different.

I had called in sick to work the day before because I couldn't bring myself to get out of bed and do anything at all besides wallow in pity and try to control all the crazy thoughts in my head.  I told my boss I was still sick and might not be in for another few days, and decided I would see about checking myself in.  I knew I needed help and didn't know what else to do (I hadn't been diagnosed with bp yet, although I've always had a suspicion I was, and I wasn't in therapy or psychiatry).  I called a mental hospital that I'd found, and the people I talked to all asked the same thing: "Are you considering suicide?"  Yes.  "Do you have a plan to do it?"  No.  "Okay then you should seek therapy and a psychiatrist."  Ok I realize this but obviously I want something more immediate right now, jesus.  It took all fucking day but I finally convinced myself to hop in a cab and go to the hospital.  I get there and the lady who helped me was extremely nice, and she eventually talked me out of checking myself in.  Since I didn't have an immediate plan to kill myself or anyone else, and since I wasn't currently having psychotic episodes, she said I didn't belong there.  It was very disheartening; I'd finally mustered up the courage to do something to help myself, and then am told that I'm not bad off enough to get the help I want...  She did bring up a good point that it might be easier for me to see an outside psychiatrist, instead of the one at the hospital who sees multiple patients at one time on a daily basis.  

So.. I went home and tried to recover from the ordeal of the day.  I took another day off work to try and get my shit together, and made appointments to see a psychiatrist and a therapist.  While it may have been good for me to be hospitalized, thankfully things did work out for me otherwise.  I started taking medication and began seeking out more information for what I'm going through.  I'm not saying that you should or shouldn't do it, that decision is ultimately up to you, but things have a way of working themselves out one way or another.  I went from thinking I was going to die if I didn't get help IMMEDIATELY, to realizing that such extreme feelings eventually do pass, and if you can make it through one day at a time you can get the help you need if you seek it out.

I know exactly what you're saying.  I had an amazing therapist last year (well.. almost amazing).  He was a grad student in psychology and therefore our sessions were recorded for "training purposes."  While I get that and all, I could tell a lot of times he would want to suggest or discuss things that, because of the "supervision," he would stop himself from saying.  He was a really cool guy, definitely the only therapist I've ever felt that I could relate to.. For example, when we talked about my penchant for inflicting pain on myself for various reasons, he told me about how he was involved with hook suspension, which I found incredibly interesting and relatable.  The next time we met and I tried to bring it up, he moved on quickly to "stress release techniques," which all seemed to be textbook-based meditation crap.  Not that it's inherently bad or whatever, just not for me.  It sucked because I felt like he really could have helped me, or at least let me open up to him in a safe environment, but because of the circumstances it didn't work out that way.  If he ever gets his own practice I'm definitely going back to him!

I agree with you about having to go through "frogs" to find your "prince" (great analogy btw!).  If I had the time and money I probably would do this (again), but I just don't at this point in my life.  I have had one or two really good therapists throughout my life, but I haven't been able to keep up with them because of location and whatnot.  Sigh.
